thread:
Claire: Heads-up — sales pushed a set of retro credits this morning labeled 'q2-experiment-refund'. Totaling ~$145K across ~28 customers. It hit Zuora and some credit memos are ready to post. Need quick guidance for month-end: restate Q2 or record as current period adjustment?

Ben: Can you confirm whether these credits reduce amounts already recognized (i.e., billed for prior consumption) or are they credits meant to cover future usage?

Claire: Sales says these are refunds for Apr/May consumption after a pricing experiment. So it's corrective, not prepaid.

Arjun: From an accounting standpoint: if it's a correction of previously recognized revenue and material, GAAP implies prior-period adjustment (restatement). If immaterial, our playbook is to book a current-period contra-revenue. What's our materiality cutoff?

Kelsey: Our internal threshold: 5% of the affected product's quarter revenue or $250k absolute. Also consider qualitative factors (audit sensitivity, customer concentration).

FinanceBot: BillingSystem: batch=2026-06-20-q2exp, credit_memos=28, total_credit=145000.00, note="q2-experiment-refund"

Ben: Ops steps I'm proposing: 1) Put manual hold on posting so NetSuite/RCS doesn't auto-adjust; 2) Map each credit memo to original invoice and revenue schedule id; 3) Compute impact by product & by quarter; 4) Decide restate vs catch-up and document rationale.

Claire: I've put holds on the credit memos and stopped automatic revenue schedule reversals.

Arjun: If we do catch-up (immaterial), typical journal example:

```
DR Sales Returns & Allowances   10,000.00
  CR Accounts Receivable         10,000.00
DR Revenue Adjustment (contra)  10,000.00
  CR Revenue                     10,000.00
```

Arjun: If it were a promo for future service (not the case), we'd record a deferred liability and amortize.

Kelsey: Claire — can you confirm contract terms for impacted customers? If most are annual with start dates > Jan, and credits cover past months, it's a correction.

Claire: Confirmed — most contracts are annual from Jan, credits apply to Apr/May usage only. So correction.

Ben: I'll pull product-level Q2 recognized revenue now and run the percent calculation. ETA ~20m.

FinanceBot: Action: holds applied by Claire at 2026-06-20T10:03:12Z; memos=[58201,58202,58210]

Ben: Calc complete — Product Beacon Q2 revenue = $1,800,000; credits tied to Beacon = $120,000 -> 6.67% of product Q2 revenue. This exceeds the 5% threshold for that product.

Arjun: That suggests a prior-period adjustment is required for Product Beacon. Next steps: accounting ops to assemble a restatement workbook with per-account GL impacts and RCS schedule diffs, reporting to draft disclosure language, and notify external auditors.

Kelsey: Agreed. Claire, please don't let the billing team post those memos. Ben, can you compile a list of revenue schedule ids and the dollar impact per schedule?

Ben: On it — I'll produce the mapping and an impact summary table within a few hours.

Claire: I'll request Sales Ops to freeze any further retro promo credits and create a simple intake form for future promos that surfaces revenue recognition risk.

Arjun: I'll prepare the restatement entry templates and sign-off checklist. We'll also flag the event in the month-end close tracker so Reporting/FP&A can include it in the quarter review.

FinanceBot: Tasks created: TASK-7781 (Hold credit memos), TASK-7782 (Schedule mapping), TASK-7783 (Restatement workbook)

Kelsey: Communication note: if we restate, we'll need to coordinate disclosure timing and auditor review — that'll add time to finalizing Q2 numbers. Keep stakeholders posted.

Claire: Thanks everyone. I'll post the mapping and keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:

Ben: Uploaded preliminary mapping to /finance/month-end/restatements/mappings.xlsx and flagged the Beacon-related memos. Will follow up with the GL impact sheet.

Arjun: Received — will incorporate into the restatement workbook and circulate for sign-off.

Kelsey: Closing the loop for now. Once audit confirms next steps, we'll update the close schedule.
